players.product: NovaSeq sequencing, BioInsight, and Billion Cell Atlas multi-omics data

connects_to.relationship: sequencers, laboratory reagents and sequencer maintenance supply

contracts.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure: Illumina is Tempus's primary supplier of sequencers and laboratory reagents, and its sole supplier of sequencers and sole provider of maintenance and repair services for them. Purchases from Illumina accounted for approximately 33%, 39% and 33% of Tempus's total vendor payments for 2025, 2024 and 2023. A June 2021 supply agreement covers sequencers, reagents, other consumables and sequencer service contracts for a 12-year term, without minimum order amounts or exclusive use of the Illumina platform; Tempus may terminate it for convenience on 90 days' prior written notice.

players.product: cloud compute and AI infrastructure for molecular and biological discovery

connects_to.relationship: Google Cloud computing, storage, data processing and networking services

contracts.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure: Tempus uses the Google Cloud Platform for a substantial portion of its computing, storage, data processing, networking and other services. In June 2020 it signed a multi-year strategic partnership with Google that included an agreement through which Tempus procures extensive cloud services from Google; the cloud agreement includes a convertible note that is reduced as Tempus procures services from Google and contemplates co-innovation projects, and Tempus signed an extension in February 2025.
contracts.units: substantial portion of computing, storage, data processing and networking

contracts.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure: Tempus has cloud agreements with both AWS and Google, and names Google and Amazon as vendors providing cloud computing services that make up substantial parts of its infrastructure.

players.product: multimodal clinical data, diagnostics, and AI applications

connects_to.relationship: multimodal foundation model delivery and data licensing

contracts.signal: Under the November 2021 Master Services Agreement, Tempus provides AstraZeneca, on a non-exclusive basis, with licensed data, sequencing, clinical trial matching, organoid modeling services, algorithm development and other products and services. In exchange for certain discounted prices, AstraZeneca has committed to spend a minimum of $220 million during the term, which continues through December 31, 2026; the minimum commitment may increase from $220 million to $320 million through December 2028 at AstraZeneca's election.
contracts.value: $220 million minimum (may increase to $320 million through December 2028 at AstraZeneca's election)
contracts.type: master services agreement (data licensing and services)

contracts.signal: In April 2025 Tempus entered into a Statement of Work with AstraZeneca under the MSA for a foundation large multimodal model in oncology: Tempus will ensure that Pathos develops, and Tempus provides AstraZeneca with, a Foundation Model developed, validated and maintained by Pathos using de-identified datasets contributed by Tempus, and AstraZeneca will pay Tempus a fee of $35 million.

quarterly_data.signal: Recursion (customer for Tempus data): Under a November 2023 Master Agreement, Tempus provides certain services and licenses data to Recursion, including a limited right to access its proprietary database of de-identified clinical and molecular data for certain therapeutic product development purposes. Recursion pays an initial license fee of $22 million and an annual license fee throughout the term, together totaling up to $160 million; the term continues through November 3, 2028, and Recursion may terminate for convenience after three years upon 90 days prior notice, subject to an early termination fee. Fees are payable in cash or Recursion Class A common stock at Recursion's option; Tempus received $32.0 million and $22.0 million in Recursion shares as payment of accounts receivable in 2025 and 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: Recursion data license up to $160 million total (initial license fee $22 million), term through November 3, 2028; $32.0 million received in Recursion shares in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: As of December 31, 2025 Tempus had signed data-business contracts with a Remaining TCV of more than $1.1 billion, including approximately $300.0 million in additional potential future contractual opt-ins; Remaining TCV includes the total potential value of its strategic collaborations with AstraZeneca and GSK. Separately, remaining performance obligations on multi-year contracts without early termination or opt-in clauses were $348.1 million, of which Tempus expects to recognize approximately 52% as revenue over the next year, 37% in year two and 11% in year three.
quarterly_data.figure: Remaining TCV more than $1.1 billion (incl. ~$300.0 million potential opt-ins); RPO $348.1 million (52% / 37% / 11%)

quarterly_data.signal: Pathos (private): under the April 2025 Pathos Master Agreement, Pathos is responsible for developing the oncology Foundation Model provided to AstraZeneca; Tempus licenses Pathos a comprehensive de-identified multi-modal dataset to train it, and Pathos will pay Tempus data license fees of $200 million over a three-year period, including a $50 million upfront payment paid as of April 2025, and will pay Tempus the first $60 million of cloud compute costs for the secure cloud environment Tempus provides to host the model. Tempus receives a license to use the completed model and will pay Pathos $35 million, of which $25 million has been paid.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 million data license fees over three years ($50 million upfront); first $60 million of cloud compute costs paid by Pathos; $35 million payable to Pathos ($25 million paid)

quarterly_data.signal: Tempus's cloud and software expense within selling, general and administrative expenses was $135,998 thousand in 2025, versus $95,401 thousand in 2024 and $85,709 thousand in 2023.
quarterly_data.figure: cloud and software expense $135,998 thousand (2025) vs $95,401 thousand (2024)

quarterly_data.signal: Microsoft: with the Paige acquisition Tempus assumed $39.5 million of remaining purchase commitments under Paige's Microsoft Azure cloud services agreement in excess of forecasted usage, recorded in other long-term liabilities.
quarterly_data.figure: $39.5 million assumed Microsoft Azure purchase commitments in excess of forecasted usage

quarterly_data.signal: SoftBank: SB Tempus Corp., a 50/50 joint venture with SoftBank Group Corporation that closed on July 18, 2024, will engage in Japan in business activities similar to Tempus's in the United States, including clinical sequencing, organizing patient data and building a real world data business; Tempus also earns income under an IP License Agreement with SB Tempus.
